question: Can a pairwise LLM-as-a-Judge be improved iteratively using only synthetic preference data, with no human preference labels?
hypothesis: Training on judgments that agree with a synthetic preference construction (a response to a modified instruction is worse for the original) yields a better evaluator, with an automatic curriculum as the model improves.
contributions: Iterative self-training scheme for LLM-as-a-Judge using only synthetic preference pairs
Llama3-70B-Instruct improved from 75.4 to 88.3 (88.7 with majority vote) on RewardBench without labeled preferences
Ablations on data source, bad-response generation, labeled-data comparison and mixing

method.summary: Pick WildChat reasoning instructions, generate a good response and a response to a modified instruction (the bad one) with Mixtral 22Bx8 Instruct, sample N=15 judgments from the current judge, keep one correct reasoning chain and verdict per example (rejection sampling against the synthetic label), and fine-tune Llama3-70B-Instruct on those; repeat, always restarting from the seed.

prompts.purpose: judgment annotation / eval (MT-Bench and RewardBench judge prompt)
prompts.text: Please act as an impartial judge and evaluate the quality of the responses provided by two AI assistants to the user question displayed below. You should choose the assistant that follows the user's instructions and answers the user's question better. Your evaluation should consider factors such as the helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, depth, creativity, and level of detail of their responses. Begin your evaluation by comparing the two responses and provide a short explanation. Avoid any position biases and ensure that the order in which the responses were presented does not influence your decision. Do not allow the length of the responses to influence your evaluation. Do not favor certain names of the assistants. Be as objective as possible. After providing your explanation, output your final verdict by strictly following this format: "[[A]]" if assistant A is better, "[[B]]" if assistant B is better.

prompts.purpose: generate worse response via modified instruction
prompts.text: Please first generate a modified instruction that is highly relevant but not semantically identical to the instruction above from the user. Then write a high-quality answer which is a good response to the modified instruction but not a good response to the original user question.
Please rewrite the Assistant's Answer to make it worse.
Firstly, categorize the instruction above into one of the following categories

limits: Authors: generative judges have longer outputs and higher inference cost than score-only reward models
Only 70B tested; no study of smaller models
Needs a capable, already-aligned instruction-tuned seed model
Only pairwise evaluation; single-response scoring left to future work
Only accuracy reported, no compute cost
Single training run per config, no confidence intervals; MT-Bench gains over seed are small (77.8 to 79.0)
Position order alone swings RewardBench by 5.6 points, so single-order numbers are not comparable
Evaluation targets are preference benchmarks (RewardBench, MT-Bench, HelpSteer2), not calibration against domain-specific human labels, no kappa or per-class error rates
Code, weights and data release not stated
